fields.meta_description: Build a candidate screening form with must-have questions, a score for every applicant, and an email to the right hiring manager. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Candidate Screening Form That Shortlists Applicants
fields.hero_description: Build a candidate screening form that scores each applicant's answers and saves every one to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens to Each Applicant's Answers
fields.features_subheading: A candidate screening form should leave the recruiter a short list to call. Each part below does one piece of that work.
fields.feature_1:
Must-have questions that sort the pool

Mark the answers a role cannot do without, such as a current forklift certification. Applicants who meet every one join the shortlist, and the rest wait for a recruiter to look.
fields.feature_2:
A point score on every applicant

Give each answer a point value and set the line for an interview, such as 70 out of 100. The app adds up the points when the form is submitted and saves the total on the record.
fields.feature_3:
Questions that change with the role

Ask a driver about license class and a cashier about weekend hours on the same form. Applicants pick the role first and then see only the questions written for that job.
fields.feature_4:
Resumes read into fields

Let applicants attach a resume beside their answers. The app reads the last employer, job title, and dates into fields, and any value it cannot read clearly goes to a person.
fields.feature_5:
An alert to the person who hires

Send each shortlisted applicant to the recruiter or manager for that role or location. Alerts go out by email, Slack, or in the app, with the answers and the score in the message.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take in-house

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can connect it to your applicant tracking system through its API or host it beside your careers page.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Hiring Desks, Four Screening Forms
fields.tab_content_1:
Forklift applicants who miss a must-have wait for review

Grisholt Distribution fills its overnight forklift shifts from a single link. Two questions are must-haves: a current forklift certification and the 10 PM to 6 AM shift. Of 64 applicants this week, 41 meet both and go on the recruiter's shortlist. The other 23 are marked Missing a must-have and wait for a person to review them.
fields.tab_content_2:
Jessamy scores 82 and lands with the hiring manager

Five answers carry the score for the inside sales role at Tansyfield Solar, and each is worth 20 points. Anyone at 70 or above goes to the hiring manager, Cormac Strandmoor. Jessamy Prudhomme scores 82. Cormac gets an email with each of her answers and the points it earned, and he books the first call from there.
fields.tab_content_3:
With a CPR card due in 18 days, Evander is flagged

Orrisdale Home Care requires a current CPR card for every home health aide, so the form asks when the card expires. A card that expires within 30 days marks the record Renewal due. Evander Thornquist's card expires in 18 days. The recruiter sees the flag and asks for the renewed card before an offer goes out.
fields.tab_content_4:
By 7:00 AM, Ilsabet has the 9 who chose Quay Street

Dunmarren Hospitality hires for 3 restaurants from one form, and each applicant picks a location. Yesterday brought 19 applicants across the group. At 7:00 AM, Ilsabet Danvik, who manages Quay Street, gets an email with the 9 who chose her restaurant. The other two managers get their own lists.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Candidate Screening Form
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to build a candidate screening form that shortlists applicants on the answers each role needs.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Tie every question to the work
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put points on the ranking questions
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the two or three things a person cannot do the job without, such as a forklift certification or a night shift. Those become must-have questions. Everything else is a preference, and preferences belong in the score instead.
fields.howto_step_2_des: EEOC guidance says what you ask before hiring should be limited to those essential for determining if a person is qualified for the job. Read each question and name the hiring decision its answer changes. Cut any question where you cannot.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the questions that rank applicants rather than rule them out, such as years in outside sales or weekend availability. Assign points to each possible answer and pick the total that earns a first call. Five questions at 20 points each make a 100-point scale.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the person who gets each shortlisted applicant: the recruiter for the role, or the manager for the location. Choose email, Slack, or an in-app alert. A busy role can send one list each morning instead of a message per applicant.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the must-haves and point values into one prompt, along with who hears about each applicant. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and a dashboard for the recruiter. Change a question or a point value later by asking for it in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit once as a strong applicant, once as someone who misses a must-have, and once just under the score line. Check that each lands with the right status and that only the first one reaches the hiring manager's inbox.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link where people apply
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the link in each job post and on your careers page, and send it to anyone who applies another way. Read through the applicants waiting for review every week, because one skipped answer should not cost you a good hire.

faq_plan.q: What is a candidate screening form?
faq_plan.a: A candidate screening form is a short set of questions an applicant answers before anyone schedules an interview. It checks the requirements a job demands, such as a certification or shift availability, and can score the rest. The recruiter then calls the applicants who fit first.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a candidate screening form?
faq_plan.a: List the must-have requirements, the questions you will score, and who should hear about each applicant. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form and the database every answer saves to. Then apply as a test candidate before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a candidate screening form ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask what decides whether you call someone: required certifications or licenses, the shifts or locations a person can work, and the earliest start date. Add two or three ranking questions, such as years in a similar job or a short answer about a past customer. Leave the full work history to the resume.

faq_plan.q: Does a candidate screening form replace a background check?
faq_plan.a: No. A screening form records what applicants tell you about their own qualifications, while a background check is a report you order later. The EEOC's guidance says the notice for that check must be in writing and in a stand-alone format, and that it can't be in an employment application. Collect that consent on a separate background check form.

faq_plan.q: What are knockout questions on a candidate screening form?
faq_plan.a: Knockout questions are the yes-or-no requirements an applicant must meet to move forward, such as holding a current forklift certification. Send anyone who misses one to a review list instead of rejecting them on the spot, because a misread question can hide a good fit. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, even in a week with hundreds of applicants.

faq_plan.q: Can a candidate screening form score applicants automatically?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Set a point value for each answer and a total that earns an interview, and the app totals each applicant's points on submit. Keep a person on every final decision, and read the answers of anyone just under the line. With Emergent, each score sits beside its answers in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What happens after an applicant passes a candidate screening form?
faq_plan.a: The recruiter or hiring manager reads the answers and books a first call or interview. During the interview, score each person on an interview evaluation form so every interviewer rates the same things. Keep the screening answers on that same record for the interviewer to read beforehand.

faq_plan.q: Which questions should a candidate screening form leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out anything that does not bear on the job. EEOC guidance says employers are explicitly prohibited from making pre-offer inquiries about disability, and that employers should not ask for a photograph of an applicant. The same guidance calls race, sex, national origin, age, and religion irrelevant to whether a person is qualified.

faq_plan.q: How long should a candidate screening form be?
faq_plan.a: Short enough to finish on a phone in a few minutes. Put the must-haves first, and let an applicant who misses one skip the scored questions. Branching by role keeps each list short, and Emergent builds it from a plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can candidate screening form answers carry over into onboarding?
faq_plan.a: Yes. When an applicant is hired, carry the contact details and certifications into the new employee form instead of asking for them twice. Keep the screening record as well. Under 29 CFR 1602.14, an employment record shall be preserved for one year from the date of the making of the record or the personnel action involved, whichever occurs later.
